notes: Lock-screen and notification forward/back now work, and they stay there. The sound in the installed app comes out of the WebView’s own audio element, and that is the media session the phone’s player follows — but the controls were only being registered with the native notification plugin, so the session the system actually hands button presses to knew about play/pause and nothing else. Every control is now registered on both sessions

The controls are re-asserted the moment a song starts. Android (and the plugin) rebuilds the notification whenever the session restarts — after a pause, after the player was released in the background, after the app reloaded — and a rebuilt session only knew the controls it was told about. That rebuild is why the buttons were “sometimes there, sometimes not”. One registration path now owns all of it (a second, older copy that registered a different set has been removed)

The player now offers 30-second jumps that actually jump 30 seconds (they used to be dead buttons: the plugin offers them, nothing listened), and “previous” follows the rule every player uses — restart the song if you are more than a few seconds in, otherwise go back a song

Battery: a paused player no longer keeps the phone awake all day. A media foreground service holds the device out of sleep for as long as it lives, so pausing and leaving the app now keeps the lock-screen controls for ten minutes and then releases the session entirely — the phone can sleep, and the next thing that plays brings the session and every control straight back

Battery: the update check no longer wakes the radio every half hour around the clock (it now waits until the app is actually open, and checks every three hours instead), a poll or heartbeat started while the app is in the background starts stopped instead of running for the whole session, and the home-screen widget poll and heartbeat were slowed from 2s/3s to 5s/6s
